text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000252's 99215 rate is well above expected in every complexity tier, including many simple visits, yet every returned 99215 chart supported the billed level, so the evidence conflicts.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding. The 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider share in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine-looking presentations such as back pain, UTI and abdominal pain (e.g., C0129314, C0129460, C0129499). The documentation points the other way. All 17 documented 99215 claims supported the billed level (e.g., C0128541, C0129614), and only 2 of the 32 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a test line on the claim, so cloned data review looks unlikely. However, the records cover only a small slice of claims, the 24% problems-signal rate and the repeated-time flags (9%) hint that notes may be built up to match the billed level, and no audit trail was received. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, such as C0128713, C0129182, C0129256 and C0129448, and check whether the documented problems and MDM fit a 0–1 condition visit for back pain or UTI. They should also obtain the EHR audit trail to rule out templated or pasted note content."}
